_comment: Player contract: bump whenever pack.ts starts emitting something an older player/game.js cannot read. The player build stamps this into public/player/build.json; publishClient refuses to publish when the two disagree, and the player refuses to boot a game.bin from a newer packer. v1 = every bundle built before the guard existed (no build.json at all) -- notably the 2026-07-22 bundle that predates terrain heightChunk/splatChunk and animation-field playback. v3 adds tilemap cell chunks: a v2 player ignores `chunk` on a tile chunk and would render an empty map with nothing logged, which is exactly the silent failure this number exists to prevent. v4 moves UI out of `scenes[].ui` and into UI nodes in the scene tree: a v3 player has no UI node classes, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse and the game renders no HUD at all, silently -- again exactly what this number exists to catch. v5 moves SHARED animation clips out of the serialized nodes and into a game-level `animations` array (with `modelAnimations` saying which model plays which), retargeted onto each character at load: a v4 player never runs that step, so every character that uses a shared clip stands in its bind pose with nothing logged. v6 moves a skinned model's per-vertex bone data (`jointIndices`/`jointWeights`) out of the manifest JSON and into blob chunks, because Model.serialize now writes those as typed arrays and a typed array stringifies as {"0":..} rather than an array: a v5 player finds neither the chunk it does not know about nor a readable array, so every skinned character loads with no bone weights and collapses to the origin -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch.
